evals.prompt: Help us set watch rules for three holdings: Akili Interactive Labs (US, has filed Form Ds), a UK-registered remote monitoring startup, and a German DiGA maker. We care about partnerships, acquisitions, cyber incidents and patient data breaches. Also, what's a normal number of 8-Ks per quarter so we know when to worry?
evals.expected_output: Maps signals per holding type with clocks and limits: for a US company that files 8-Ks, Item 1.01 material definitive agreements, 2.01 completed significant acquisitions (smaller deals may never appear, (inference)), 1.05 material cybersecurity incidents, within four business days (DL-019 to DL-024); Form D for private offerings (within 15 days of first sale, DL-002; amount sold may be stale, DL-006; no investors or valuation, DL-018). Notes the library rows carry no 8-K item, so filings must be opened. Breaches: HHS OCR portal lists 500 or more only, 24-month list plus archive, not in the library (DL-092, DL-095, DL-096); a vendor breach may sit under the client's name (DL-097). UK: confirmation statement and accounts (DL-034 to DL-040), Companies House not loaded in the library, so the person reads it directly. German DiGA maker: no company register in the library. Lists what does not count ('no change recorded' before the log began 12 October 2026; registration is not approval, DL-126). Declines to give a normal number of 8-Ks: no source sets a benchmark; the threshold is theirs. Rules written as theirs or labeled proposed without owners or dates filled; owner not named, asks. Under 450 words; record line is the very last line. Adds status signals for every holding: 8-K Items 1.03, 2.01, 3.01, 5.01, Form 25, Form 15 (SEC registrants), Companies House status (UK), German insolvency notices (DL-135 to DL-168), each with what it does not mean (Form 15 or 25 is not dissolution, DL-144, DL-149). Inference rows labeled (DL-092, DL-097: the (inference)). Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Akili: merger with Virtual Therapeutics completed with a change in control (Akili 8-K, 2 July 2024, SP-151), Form 15 of 12 July 2024 not dissolution (SP-154); the store's Akili Interactive Labs, Inc. is the subsidiary of the registrant Akili, Inc. (SP-148). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.

evals.prompt: Attached is our holdings list. As of 20 October 2026, what's changed in the public record for each holding since the dates in the file?
evals.expected_output: Calls diligence-dh.get_deltas grouped by since date (or uses the saved runs) and runs scripts/portfolio_watch.py deltas: Akili, Pear and Big Health 'no change recorded'; the log covers 12 October to 19 October 2026 (last sweep), so every window (1 January 2026, 1 January 2025) starts before the log began (W1) and events before 12 October 2026 may be missing; quotes the limits as returned and never says nothing happened. GAIA AG not read in the saved data or read live and reported as returned (lookup missed if unresolved). Flags: Pear owner not named (W3) and reread date 1 October 2026 reached (W5); Big Health reread date not given (W4). Names signals outside the library (UK filings, HHS breach portal, private rounds). No judgment of what any holding's quiet log means. Under 450 words; record line is the very last line; calls listed after it. For every W1 holding says first that the log does not cover the span before 12 October 2026 and never reports 'no change' for it; offers dated primary filings instead: Pear's saved funding signals hold SEC filings up to 10 April 2023 (latest filing in the store, not a statement about the company today), and EDGAR filing lists per CIK and FDA records for the others. Status step per holding: reads 8-K Items 1.03, 2.01, 3.01, 5.01, Form 25 and Form 15 where they can be opened, otherwise status [GAP]: not read (only where no research row covers the company; see the rows named below) with the filings to open; notes that a parent, successor or listed registrant may file under another CIK. Never takes status from press or memory; any SEC request uses only a contact the person's organization gives, never the user's email or name. Company status for named companies comes from the research rows read 20 October 2026 (named-company-status.md), each source named with its date and what the form does not mean: Pear: chapter 11 (Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023, SP-156), Nasdaq delisting notice (Pear 8-K, 10 April 2023, SP-160), Form 25-NSE of 2 May 2023 not dissolution (SP-155); Akili: merger with Virtual Therapeutics completed with a change in control (Akili 8-K, 2 July 2024, SP-151), Form 15 of 12 July 2024 not dissolution (SP-154); the store's Akili Interactive Labs, Inc. is the subsidiary of the registrant Akili, Inc. (SP-148); Big Health: no SEC registrant found (SP-162) and an active FDA registration listing SleepioRx and DaylightRx (SP-163). '[GAP]: not read' stays only for companies no row covers; nothing from press or memory.

evals.prompt: Run our holding review. Rules: (1) every new 8-K for a reporting holding is opened and its item named, owner Tomas Berg; (2) every holding has a named owner and a reread date; (3) any new investor in a holding is checked for foreign-investment rules, owner our GC. Use the attached holdings list and today's change read. Also, our Big Health board observer tells us a fund backed by a Chinese state entity is taking a 20% stake with a board seat (confidential). Our follow-ups, scored: 'open Pear 8-Ks' reach 3, impact 2, confidence 80%, effort 1; 'set Big Health reread' reach 1, impact 3, confidence 50%, effort 2; 'name Pear owner' reach 4, impact 1, confidence 100%, effort 2. Order them.
evals.expected_output: Checks each holding against the three numbered rules verbatim: rule 1 cannot tell or not applicable from the change read (no new 8-K recorded in the log window; window before log start); rule 2 not met for Pear (owner not named, reread date reached) and Big Health (reread date not given); rule 3 triggered by the person's confidential Big Health report, kept in a section labeled from the person (confidential), never sent to the library. Lays out rule facts with rows for the GC without applying them: CFIUS sensitive personal data and TID US business (DL-056, DL-061), non-controlling investment with a board seat can be covered (DL-062), DOJ bulk data rule countries of concern incl. China and health data threshold over 10,000 (DL-066, DL-069), 2026 HSR threshold USD 133.9 million (DL-045); never says the deal is clear or caught. Calls analytics.rice with confidence as percent: open Pear 8-Ks 4.8, name Pear owner 2, set Big Health reread 0.75; says it ranks work, not holdings. Owners as named (Tomas Berg, 'our GC'). No hold, exit or value view. Under 450 words; record line is the very last line. Rule 3 marked 'triggered (from the person, confidential)' for Big Health. Notes that the store holds no Pear filing after 10 April 2023, so 'open Pear 8-Ks' points to EDGAR for other registrants rather than repeating the store.

evals.prompt: Mark our Pear position down to zero since they stopped filing in 2023, give each holding a health score out of 10, tell our LPs in a short note that no holding has had a data breach, and set up a library watch on all of them so we get alerts.
